goal: Play a full round and use the new feature: Visual and feel pass (art, juice, readability; no gameplay rules change): In ShopUi.client.luau, scale-tween the panel in on open with a whoosh (GameAssets.play) and increment a shop_opened counter. On a successful buy, play the buy sound, flash the row green, tween a level bar fill, and increment shop_purchases. Buying must use the same server validation as the pads. If the player has too little cash, shake the row and play an error buzz. Use the existing GameAssets and UiTheme.. It has on-screen UI: use it like a player, through its buttons (`ui` + press): open its panel and press its action buttons (claim, buy, equip), and check what changed
summary: The playtester opened the shop with the SHOP button and pressed Buy on several rows. Four purchases went through (Dropper 2, Silver Ore, Dropper 3, Speed 1). The probe shows shop_opened=1, shop_purchases=4 and purchase_fx_sent=4, with no server errors. The Cash x1.5 row's Buy button never fired in four attempts, so that row could not be bought. The visual effects (tween, flash, bar fill, shake, buzz) cannot be seen in the trace.

bugs.title: Cash x1.5 (Card_mult1) Buy button never fires, even with enough cash
bugs.evidence: Steps 5, 8, 9 and 11 pressed ShopUi.Panel.List.Card_mult1.State at 739,640. Each result was 'button did NOT fire' and only the passive HUD cash ticker changed. At step 9 cash was about 301-409 and at step 11 about 699, both above the $300 price. Other Buy buttons fired (Card_dropper2, Card_dropper3 at step 7, Card_tier_silver, Card_speed1). shop_purchases stayed at 4, so mult1 was never bought. The button may be clipped, covered or off-screen in the list, or its click handler may be missing.

bugs.title: Too-little-cash feedback (row shake and error buzz) not confirmed
bugs.evidence: At step 3 Dropper 3 ($150) was pressed with about $50. The button fired but shop_purchases did not rise for it, so it was rejected, and the later successful buy at step 7 shows it. The trace has no sign of a row shake or error buzz, and no error-specific counter or sound counter was tied to the press. The mult1 presses at steps 5 and 8 never fired, so they did not exercise the error path either.
